statement: An allowed modification of grid is either grid itself or a matrix M obtained by choosing exactly one index (i,j) with grid[i][j] = 0 and setting M[i][j] = 1 while leaving every other entry equal to grid. For any such M, let L(M) be 0 if M has no cell equal to 1, and otherwise the maximum size of a maximal set of cells with M = 1 that is connected by moves up, down, left, or right, where size is the number of cells. Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, r = max { L(M) : M is an allowed modification of grid }.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, largest_island(grid) returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, access out of bounds, or panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, 1 <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, r <= n*n.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, r = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1. Also n = 1.

statement: Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, r = n*n.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1. Also grid[i][j] = 1 for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n.

statement: An original island is a maximal nonempty set C of cells such that grid[i][j] = 1 for all (i,j) in C and any two cells of C can be joined by a path in C moving only up, down, left, or right. Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, for every original island C, r >= |C|, where |C| is the number of cells in C.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: An original island is a maximal nonempty set C of cells such that grid[i][j] = 1 for all (i,j) in C and any two cells of C can be joined by a path in C moving only up, down, left, or right. For a zero cell z = (i,j) with grid[i][j] = 0, let Adj(z) be the set of distinct original islands that contain at least one cell orthogonally adjacent to z. Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, for every zero cell z, r >= 1 + sum over C in Adj(z) of |C|.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Call M an allowed modification of grid if M is either grid itself or obtained by changing exactly one 0-cell of grid to 1. Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, there exist an allowed modification M and a maximal set C of cells with M = 1, connected by moves up, down, left, or right, such that |C| = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Call M an allowed modification of grid if M is either grid itself or obtained by changing exactly one 0-cell of grid to 1. Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, for every allowed modification M and every maximal set C of cells with M = 1 connected by moves up, down, left, or right, |C| <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever largest_island(A) returns a result rA and largest_island(B) returns a result rB, rA <= rB.
preconditions: Let n = len(A). Both A and B are n x n binary matrices satisfying the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(A[i]) = len(B[i]) = n; for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, A[i][j] and B[i][j] are each either 0 or 1; and A[i][j] <= B[i][j] for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Let G^T be the n x n matrix with G^T[i][j] = grid[j][i] for all 0 <= i,j < n. Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r and largest_island(G^T) returns a result rT, r = rT.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Let G' be the n x n matrix with G'[i][j] = grid[n-1-i][n-1-j] for all 0 <= i,j < n. Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r and largest_island(G') returns a result r', r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, r = 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1. Also n >= 2, and there is exactly one pair (i,j) with grid[i][j] = 1; every other entry is 0.

statement: Whenever largest_island(grid) returns a result r, r >= 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1. Also n >= 2, and there exists at least one cell with value 1 and at least one cell with value 0.

statement: Let an original island be a maximal nonempty 4-connected set of 1-cells of grid, and for a zero cell z let Adj(z) be the set of distinct original islands containing a cell orthogonally adjacent to z. If grid has at least one 0, then whenever largest_island(grid) returns r, r = max( max { |C| : C is an original island } (taking this maximum as 0 when there are no original islands), max { 1 + sum over C in Adj(z) of |C| : z is a zero cell } ). If grid has no 0, then r = n*n.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.
